claims.text: RHEAs exhibit superior high-temperature mechanical strength because high-mixing-entropy-induced lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
RHEAs exhibit altered thermoelastic behavior because high-mixing-entropy-induced lattice distortions modify phonon scattering.
MoNbTaW can serve as a homogeneous, single-phase refractory HEA for the proposed comparison.
A conventional refractory alloy with lower mixing entropy will have reduced lattice distortion relative to the RHEA.
Neutron or synchrotron in situ diffraction can monitor lattice distortion and associated phonon behavior during high-temperature testing.
High mixing entropy drives lattice distortions in the RHEA.
The lattice distortions act as barriers to dislocation glide.
The lattice distortions alter phonon transport.
The multi-principal-element configuration produces large local lattice strains.
Impeded dislocation motion increases the RHEA's yield strength.
Altered phonon scattering produces a modified elastic response under thermal stress.
The RHEA will have higher high-temperature yield strength than the conventional refractory-alloy baseline.
The RHEA will exhibit a delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to the baseline.
The RHEA will exhibit distinct thermoelastic moduli and retain stiffness at high temperature relative to the baseline.
Diffraction will reveal significantly greater lattice distortion in the RHEA, correlated with its mechanical and elastic anomalies.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from 1000 to 1500°C when grain size and phase homogeneity are controlled and oxidation and phase separation are minimized.
Secondary-phase formation or ordering at extreme temperatures could affect the observed mechanical and thermoelastic behavior.
